instructions.text:
French law from Légifrance through the official PISTE API (read-only): consolidated laws and decrees (LODA), codes (CODE), Cour de cassation and courts of appeal (JURI), Conseil constitutionnel (CONSTIT), Conseil d'État and administrative courts (CETAT), CNIL deliberations (CNIL), collective labour agreements (KALI) and company agreements (ACCO). Use them for any question on French law or case law.

## Workflow
1. Find: `fr_search` searches one fond, paged with `page` and `has_more`; `fr_search_all` returns a few hits from several fonds. `fr_resolve` turns a free-text citation (code article, law number, ECLI, case number) into Legifrance ids.
2. Read by id prefix: LEGITEXT -> `fr_get_act` (metadata and table of contents); LEGIARTI or KALIARTI -> `fr_get_text`; JURITEXT, CONSTEXT or CETATEXT -> `fr_get_decision`; CNILTEXT -> `fr_get_deliberation`; KALITEXT -> `fr_get_convention`; ACCOTEXT -> `fr_get_company_agreement` (metadata only: the full text is a .docx on Légifrance).
3. Check and navigate: `fr_verify_citations` checks every citation of a draft against the official record; `fr_get_related` lists what an article or a decision cites or is cited by; `fr_diff_article` compares two versions of an article.
4. Limits: `fr_coverage` says what this server does not cover and whether it runs on the PISTE sandbox.

## Long texts
`fr_get_text`, `fr_get_decision` and `fr_get_deliberation` return a short summary by default. A summary is never the whole text: pass `detail="full"` before quoting a threshold, amount or rate; while `next_offset` is present, call again with `offset` set to it. To reach the relevant part directly, pass `focus` with a few words: you get the best passages and their `offset`.

## Hard rules
- Cite every source with its `citation` and `source_url`; for case law add the `ecli` when present.
- Never invent an id, an ECLI, an ELI or a citation: take each one from tool output. Many CAA and TA decisions have no ECLI.
- ELI: none from the API for legislation. `source_url` is the stable Légifrance page, not an ELI; an `eli` field appears only when the API provides one.
- Attribution: Source : Légifrance / DILA — Licence Ouverte 2.0. When you reuse the data, give this source and the consultation date (`consulted_on` in `fr_coverage`).
- Versions default to today's date in Paris; to get the law in force on another day, pass `date` to `fr_get_act` (`version_date` in `fr_search`) as YYYY-MM-DD, then read the article ids of that version with `fr_get_text`. Texts are verbatim (table cells are joined with " | "): this server does not decide whether a provision applies to a case.
- `etat`: VIGUEUR, VIGUEUR_ETEN, VIGUEUR_NON_ETEN, ABROGE_DIFF in force; VIGUEUR_DIFF not yet; MODIFIE, ABROGE, PERIME no longer; DENONCE may still apply (list: `etat` field).
- An empty result does not mean the law is silent: call `fr_coverage` and tell the user what is missing.

## Errors
A failed call returns isError with a text that starts with a code:
- `[invalid_arg]` an argument is missing or malformed: fix it as the message says.
- `[not_found]` nothing exists for that id: search again.
- `[rate_limited]` PISTE quota reached: wait the delay given, then retry.
- `[upstream_error]` Légifrance/PISTE failure: retry if the message asks, else report it.
- `[config_error]` credentials or settings are missing or rejected: ask the user to fix the configuration.
- `[audit_error]` the local audit log could not be written, so the result was withheld: tell the user.

arguments.description: Identifiant Légifrance de la décision (JURITEXT…, CETATEXT… ou CONSTEXT…).

descriptor.description: Établir l'état du droit français en vigueur sur une question, sources officielles à l'appui (la question est demandée au tour suivant).
descriptor.name: etat_du_droit
descriptor.title: État du droit

descriptor.description: Vérifier les citations juridiques d'un texte contre Légifrance (le texte est demandé au tour suivant).
descriptor.name: verifier_citations

descriptor.description: The metadata and the nested table of contents of one consolidated text, by its LEGITEXT identifier (with an optional _DD-MM-YYYY version suffix), as Markdown. At most 500 entries.
descriptor.name: act
descriptor.title: Law, decree or code (table of contents)

descriptor.description: The full text of one consolidated article, by its LEGIARTI identifier, as Markdown. At most 40,000 characters; a last line gives the offset to resume with fr_get_text.
descriptor.name: article
descriptor.title: Article (full text)

descriptor.description: The full text of one article of a code, by the code slug (code-civil, code-du-travail...) and the article number (L. 1234-5), in force today in Paris, as Markdown. Complete the code variable to list the slugs.
descriptor.name: code_article
descriptor.title: Code article by number

descriptor.description: The full text of one court decision, by its JURITEXT, CETATEXT or CONSTEXT identifier, as Markdown, with the official summary. At most 40,000 characters; a last line gives the offset to resume with fr_get_decision.
descriptor.name: decision
descriptor.title: Court decision (full text)

descriptor.description: What this server covers, how it is sourced and what it does NOT cover, with the PISTE environment and the state of the configuration (the same object as the fr_coverage tool).
descriptor.name: coverage
descriptor.title: Coverage and known gaps

descriptor.description: Describe what this server covers, how it is sourced and what it does NOT cover. Call it before telling a user that the law "does not contain" something, and whenever a search comes back empty: the gap may be in this server, not in the law. Each gap comes with a fallback. It also reports the PISTE environment (sandbox or production), whether the configuration is complete, the data source and licence with today's consultation date, and the note on ELI identifiers. No arguments, no network call.
descriptor.name: fr_coverage
descriptor.title: Coverage and known gaps

descriptor.description: Compare the versions of a code or law article (LEGIARTI) in force on `date_a` and `date_b` (YYYY-MM-DD; `date_b` defaults to today in Paris). Returns both versions with their validity dates and `etat`, and a compact word-level diff: removed and added passages with a little context. `date_fin` is the day the next version (or the repeal) takes effect, absent when there is no end date; `etat` is the Légifrance code (ABROGE_DIFF: still in force, repeal scheduled). `identical` is true when both dates fall in the same version. To read a single version use fr_get_text.

article_id.description: A LEGIARTI... id of any version of the article.

date_b.description: Second date YYYY-MM-DD (default: today in Paris).

descriptor.name: fr_diff_article
descriptor.title: Compare article versions

annotations.title: Read a law, decree or code

descriptor.description: Read a consolidated law, decree or code by its LEGITEXT id (from fr_search on LODA or CODE): metadata, citation, source_url and a table of contents of sections and articles with their `article_id`. Returns the version in force on `date` (YYYY-MM-DD; default: the version named by a suffixed text_id, else today in Paris); without `date_fin_version` that version has no end date. The table of contents is paged: up to `toc_limit` entries (default 100) from `toc_offset`; continue with `next_toc_offset`. It does not return article text: read an article with fr_get_text. For a collective agreement (KALITEXT) use fr_get_convention.

date.description: Version date YYYY-MM-DD (default: the version named by a suffixed text_id, else today in Paris).

text_id.description: A LEGITEXT... id (from fr_search on LODA or CODE).

descriptor.name: fr_get_act

etat.description: In force: VIGUEUR, VIGUEUR_ETEN, VIGUEUR_NON_ETEN, ABROGE_DIFF. Not yet: VIGUEUR_DIFF. DENONCE may still apply. Every code is classed in the etat of fr_get_text.

next_toc_offset.description: Pass as toc_offset to read the next page; absent on the last page.

title.description: Omitted when citation already contains it.

etat.description: Omitted when equal to the etat of the text.

descriptor.title: Read a law, decree or code

descriptor.description: Read a company-level agreement (accord d'entreprise) by its ACCOTEXT id from fr_search on fond ACCO. Returns METADATA ONLY: company, SIRET, IDCC, APE code, sector, themes, signatory unions, dates, citation and source_url. Légifrance distributes the full text only as a .docx attachment, which this tool does not return: point the user to source_url.

agreement_id.description: An ACCOTEXT... id (from fr_search on fond ACCO).

descriptor.name: fr_get_company_agreement
descriptor.title: Read a company agreement (metadata)

descriptor.description: Read a collective labour agreement text (convention collective, avenant, annexe) by its KALITEXT id from fr_search on fond KALI: title, IDCC, parent convention, status, citation, source_url and a table of contents. Article entries carry KALIARTI ids: read them with fr_get_text. Page the table of contents with `toc_offset`/`toc_limit` (default 100) and `next_toc_offset`. For a company-level agreement use fr_get_company_agreement.

convention_id.description: A KALITEXT... id (from fr_search on fond KALI).

descriptor.name: fr_get_convention

next_toc_offset.description: Pass as toc_offset to read the next page; absent on the last page.

title.description: Omitted when citation already contains it.

etat.description: Omitted when equal to the etat of the text.

descriptor.title: Read a collective agreement

descriptor.description: Read a court decision by id: JURITEXT (Cour de cassation, courts of appeal), CONSTEXT (Conseil constitutionnel) or CETATEXT (Conseil d'État, administrative courts), as found by fr_search. Returns court, formation, solution, case numbers, date, the native `ecli` when Légifrance has one (never invented), citation and source_url. By default it adds a short `summary`: the official summary when published, else the operative part or the beginning of the text; a short decision comes back whole in `text`. Use `detail`="full" with `offset`/`max_chars` (default 4,000 characters) to read the text page by page (follow `next_offset`), or `focus` to get the best matching passages (default 3).

decision_id.description: A JURITEXT..., CONSTEXT... or CETATEXT... id (from fr_search on JURI, CONSTIT or CETAT).

detail.description: "summary" (default): metadata and a short summary. "full": the text from offset, up to max_chars.

focus.description: A few words: return the best matching passages instead of the summary or window.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters of text returned (500 to 40000).

offset.description: Start position in characters for detail="full"; pass the next_offset of the previous call.

passages.description: Number of passages returned with focus.

descriptor.name: fr_get_decision

next_offset.description: Pass as offset to read the next window.

score.description: BM25 relevance, only comparable between the passages of this answer.

summary_truncated.description: True when the summary itself is cut short or is only the opening of the text. Absent for an official summary or operative part that is given whole (it may still cover only part of the text).

title.description: Omitted when citation already contains it.

descriptor.title: Read a court decision

descriptor.description: Read a CNIL deliberation or decision by its CNILTEXT id (from fr_search on fond CNIL): number, nature (e.g. Sanction), status, dates, citation and source_url. By default a text of about 1,200 characters or less comes back whole in `text` and a longer one as a `summary`: the operative part of a sanction or formal notice, else the beginning of the text. `detail`="full" pages through the text with `offset`/`max_chars` (default 4,000 characters) and `next_offset`; `focus` returns the most relevant passages (default 3) and takes precedence over `detail` and `offset`. Personal data is redacted by the CNIL in published texts.

deliberation_id.description: A CNILTEXT... id (from fr_search on fond CNIL).

detail.description: "summary" (default): metadata and a short summary. "full": the text from offset, up to max_chars.

focus.description: A few words: return the best matching passages instead of the summary or window.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters of text returned (500 to 40000).

offset.description: Start position in characters for detail="full"; pass the next_offset of the previous call.

passages.description: Number of passages returned with focus.

descriptor.name: fr_get_deliberation

next_offset.description: Pass as offset to read the next window.

score.description: BM25 relevance, only comparable between the passages of this answer.

summary_truncated.description: True when the summary itself is cut short or is only the opening of the text. Absent for an official summary or operative part that is given whole (it may still cover only part of the text).

title.description: Omitted when citation already contains it.

descriptor.title: Read a CNIL deliberation

descriptor.description: List the legal links of an article (LEGIARTI) or a decision (JURITEXT, CONSTEXT, CETATEXT): texts it cites, texts citing it, and case law it refers to. Article links come from Légifrance with their ids; decision links are parsed from the decision's references, have no id and may carry an inexact code: pass one to fr_resolve only if its citation names a code. Each link has a `relation`, a `citation` and, when known, an `id` and `source_url`; `relation` as a parameter keeps one kind of link. At most 100 links are returned: `truncated` is true when there are more, and there is no next page.

id.description: A LEGIARTI... article id or a JURITEXT..., CONSTEXT... or CETATEXT... decision id.

relation.description: Only the links of this relation: cites or cited_by for an article, cites_case_law or applies_text for a decision; the other family is refused. Omit it to get them all. The filter is applied before the 100-link cap, and total counts the links of that relation.

descriptor.name: fr_get_related
descriptor.title: Related texts and decisions

descriptor.description: Read one article by id: LEGIARTI (from fr_get_act or a CODE search hit) or KALIARTI (from fr_get_convention). Returns its citation (for example "Code civil, art. 9"), source_url, status, validity dates and parent code or text. By default (`detail`="summary") an article of up to 2,000 characters comes back whole and a longer one as a summary of about 1,200 characters (`summary_truncated` is true when the summary stops before the end of the text). A summary is never the whole text: use `detail`="full" before quoting a threshold, amount or rate; it returns up to `max_chars` (default 4,000) from `offset`, and `next_offset` tells where to continue; `focus` returns the most relevant passages instead (default 3). Each LEGIARTI id is one version of the article: `date_debut` and `date_fin` bound its validity; without `date_fin` it has no end date, and without `date_debut` its entry into force is not set yet (see `etat`).

article_id.description: A LEGIARTI... id (from fr_get_act or a CODE hit) or a KALIARTI... id (from fr_get_convention).

detail.description: "summary" (default): metadata and a short summary. "full": the text from offset, up to max_chars.

focus.description: A few words: return the best matching passages instead of the summary or window.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters of text returned (500 to 40000).

offset.description: Start position in characters for detail="full"; pass the next_offset of the previous call.

passages.description: Number of passages returned with focus.

descriptor.name: fr_get_text

date_debut.description: Omitted when the entry into force is not set yet (see etat).

date_fin.description: Omitted when the article is in force without an end date.

etat.description: In force: VIGUEUR, VIGUEUR_ETEN, VIGUEUR_NON_ETEN, ABROGE_DIFF. Not yet in force: VIGUEUR_DIFF (deferred entry, date_debut may be absent). No longer in force: MODIFIE, ABROGE, PERIME, ANNULE, REMPLACE, TRANSFERE, SUBSTITUE, DISJOINT, MODIFIE_MORT_NE (never in force: modified before taking effect). DENONCE: denounced, may still apply during notice and survival (Labour Code, article L2261-10). INITIALE, SANS_ETAT: no signal.

next_offset.description: Pass as offset to read the next window.

parent_id.description: LEGITEXT or KALITEXT of the parent text.

score.description: BM25 relevance, only comparable between the passages of this answer.

summary_truncated.description: True when the summary itself is cut short or is only the opening of the text. Absent for an official summary or operative part that is given whole (it may still cover only part of the text).

descriptor.title: Read an article

descriptor.description: Turn one free-text legal citation into Légifrance ids, for example "article 1240 du code civil", "loi n° 78-17 du 6 janvier 1978", "Cass. civ. 1re, 4 juin 2025, n° 24-13.470" or an ECLI. Returns `candidates` (id, kind, citation, source_url, confidence high/medium/low), best first; nothing is guessed or fabricated, and an empty list comes with a `note` saying why. Pass `date` (YYYY-MM-DD, default: today in Paris) for the article version in force on that day. Then open a candidate with the fr_get_* tool for its kind; to check all citations of a text at once use fr_verify_citations.

citation.description: One citation in free text, e.g. "art. L. 1234-5 du code du travail" or an ECLI.

date.description: Date YYYY-MM-DD for the article version (default: today in Paris).

descriptor.name: fr_resolve

date_debut.description: First day of this version, YYYY-MM-DD.

date_fin.description: Day the next version (or the repeal) takes effect; absent: no known end.

etat.description: In force: VIGUEUR, VIGUEUR_ETEN, VIGUEUR_NON_ETEN, ABROGE_DIFF. Not yet: VIGUEUR_DIFF. DENONCE may still apply. Every code is classed in the etat of fr_get_text.

descriptor.title: Resolve a legal citation

descriptor.description: Keyword search in one Légifrance fond (default LODA): laws and decrees (LODA), codes (CODE), case law (JURI, CONSTIT, CETAT), CNIL deliberations (CNIL), collective agreements (KALI) or company agreements (ACCO). Returns one page of hits (default 10) with id, title, snippet, citation and source_url; ask for the next `page` while `has_more`. `match` defaults to any word: use `all` for several words, `exact` for a phrase, fr_resolve for one known article. `date_from`/`date_to` filter by date; for KALI, `in_force_only` keeps the texts in force (not their articles' status). LODA and CODE hits are the versions in force on `version_date` (default: today in Paris); a hit `date` is the date Légifrance gives for that fond, not always the act date. Open a hit with the fr_get_* tool for its id prefix (LEGITEXT: fr_get_act, JURITEXT/CONSTEXT/CETATEXT: fr_get_decision, CNILTEXT: fr_get_deliberation, KALITEXT: fr_get_convention, ACCOTEXT: fr_get_company_agreement); CODE hits list `articles`.

in_force_only.description: KALI only: keep texts in force (VIGUEUR, VIGUEUR_ETEN, VIGUEUR_NON_ETEN), drop DENONCE, MODIFIE, PERIME, REMPLACE, ABROGE. DENONCE excluded, though it may still apply during notice. It filters texts, not the status of their articles.

match.description: "any": any word (default); "all": all words; "exact": exact phrase.

query.description: Free-text query, e.g. "republique numerique". AND/OR/NOT/~/^ are unreliable; a dangling one fails the search. Trailing * is a wildcard.

version_date.description: LODA and CODE only: version in force on this date, YYYY-MM-DD (default today, Paris).

descriptor.name: fr_search

ArticleView.description: Un article trouvé dans un résultat de code.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD as Légifrance gives it for the fond (CNIL: publication, ACCO: signature), not always the act date; absent if unknown.

etat.description: In force: VIGUEUR, VIGUEUR_ETEN, VIGUEUR_NON_ETEN, ABROGE_DIFF. Not yet: VIGUEUR_DIFF. DENONCE may still apply. Every code is classed in the etat of fr_get_text.

id.description: Identifiant sans suffixe de version ; son préfixe désigne l'outil de lecture.

idcc.description: IDCC (KALI et ACCO), à partir de la v0.2.

kind.description:
Fond du résultat, en minuscules : `loda`, `code`, `juri`, `constit`, `cetat`, `cnil`,
`kali` ou `acco`.

title.description: Titre, s'il n'est pas déjà dans `citation`.

has_more.description: True if a next page exists and is reachable.

hits.description: Résultats, dans l'ordre de l'API ; toujours présents, même vides.

note.description: Hint: no match, window end, articles to page, or content removed.

total.description: Total results; for CODE, codes; total_articles (if present) counts articles.

total_articles.description: Nombre total d'articles correspondants (fond `CODE`), à partir de la v0.2.

descriptor.title: Search Légifrance

descriptor.description: Search several Légifrance fonds at once (default LODA, CODE, JURI, CETAT, CONSTIT) and return the top `per_fond` hits of each (default 3, max 10), grouped by fond with their totals. Use it for a first overview when you do not know where the answer is; then refine with fr_search on the relevant fond, which supports paging and filters. A fond that fails yields an error entry without failing the others.

fonds.description: Fonds to search (default LODA, CODE, JURI, CETAT, CONSTIT).

query.description: Free-text query. AND/OR/NOT/~/^ are unreliable; a dangling one fails the search. Trailing * is a wildcard.

descriptor.name: fr_search_all

has_more.description: True if fr_search can page further in this fond.

note.description: Hint: no match, or content removed.

descriptor.title: Search several fonds

descriptor.description: Check every legal citation found in a text of up to 20,000 characters, for example a draft answer, against the official Légifrance record. Recognises code articles (a bare number needs article/art.; one prefixed by L, R or D does not), laws and decrees, court decisions, ECLI, CNIL deliberations and collective agreements; found=0 does not prove that a text cites nothing. For each citation returns its `span`, a `status` (verified, not_found, ambiguous, unresolvable or invalid), the official record when found and a `note` explaining any mismatch; `verified` means the article exists, not that it says what the draft claims. A quoted excerpt is compared with the official text (`quote`) only when it is glued to the citation: no `quote` means NOT checked. It checks the first `max_citations` (default 50); if `truncated` is true, call again on the rest of the text. Use it before giving the user an answer that cites law; for a single citation fr_resolve is lighter.

max_citations.description: Maximum citations checked, in order of appearance.

text.description: The text whose citations must be checked (up to 20000 characters).

descriptor.name: fr_verify_citations

quote.description: match or quote_mismatch. Only for an excerpt glued to the citation; absent: not checked.

date_debut.description: First day of this version, YYYY-MM-DD.

date_fin.description: Day the next version (or the repeal) takes effect; absent: no known end.

etat.description: In force: VIGUEUR, VIGUEUR_ETEN, VIGUEUR_NON_ETEN, ABROGE_DIFF. Not yet: VIGUEUR_DIFF. DENONCE may still apply. Every code is classed in the etat of fr_get_text.

descriptor.title: Verify legal citations
